scope: All 132 stored BMO1 statements (2005-2026). Full-statement thematic review; not solution certification or original-source verification. No referenced figures.
rationale_policy: Rationale required for changes and mixed classifications. Clear unchanged single-topic cases record the exact reviewed statement, hash, date and category. Earlier rationale records are retained.

uk1.2005.0.1.rationale: The money transfers give linear equations subject to positive integer constraints on n and the holdings.

uk1.2005.0.3.rationale: A two-colouring must force a monochromatic additive relation between integers.

uk1.2005.0.5.rationale: Rational transformations generate all reduced fractions using numerator/denominator arithmetic.

uk1.2006.0.4.rationale: The triangle defines an adjacency graph of cells; the route asks for a maximum simple path, without a metric geometry claim.

uk1.2006.0.6.rationale: Count containing triangles modulo two in a geometric point configuration.

uk1.2007.0.3.rationale: This counts digit permutations with relative-order restrictions; digits serve as distinct labels, with no arithmetic constraint.

uk1.2008.0.1.rationale: Evaluation uses algebraic factorisation of fourth and second powers.

uk1.2008.0.4.rationale: A large integer subset forces a pair of complementary residue classes modulo eight.

uk1.2008.0.5.rationale: A product of geometric segment ratios is optimised under the interior-point constraint.

uk1.2008.0.6.rationale: A recursively defined function has an integer-value assertion and a count of arithmetic equality cases.

uk1.2009.0.5.rationale: A rational quadratic recurrence must have a repeated orbit value; rational denominator behaviour is essential.

uk1.2009.0.6.rationale: An algebraic/trigonometric inequality is constrained by an obtuse triangle.

uk1.2010.0.6.rationale: Uniqueness of integer solutions is governed by the two quadratic expressions and integer differences.

uk1.2011.0.1.rationale: An average equation determines an integer deletion through integrality constraints.

uk1.2011.0.2.rationale: An integer-length drilled solid gives a volume/surface Diophantine condition.

uk1.2011.0.6.rationale: A polynomial bound on triangle sides is combined with their triangle inequalities and fixed pair-product sum.

uk1.2012.0.4.rationale: Integer transfer and multiplication operations require arithmetic reachability invariants.

uk1.2012.0.5.rationale: The claim excludes an equality between products of consecutive integers.

uk1.2014.0.1.rationale: A numerical rational expression is simplified using polynomial factorisation.

uk1.2014.0.5.rationale: Perpendicular projections in an equilateral triangle give length and area identities. Real-variable algebra is not the stated subject.

uk1.2014.0.6.rationale: A weighted side/angle expression is bounded by triangle constraints.

uk1.2015.0.1.rationale: Ordering exponential expressions requires comparisons of powers and exponents.

uk1.2015.0.4.rationale: An algebraic recurrence for x^n+x^(-n) is combined with integer divisibility.

uk1.2015.0.6.rationale: An integer-valued functional condition preserves Egyptian-fraction identities.

uk1.2016.0.1.rationale: Calendar indices specify counts of books and shelves; the substantive condition is integer divisibility, not counting arrangements.

uk1.2016.0.6.rationale: Distinct representations are built from integers with restricted prime factors.

uk1.2017.0.1.rationale: Count odd decimal digits by position in an integer interval.

uk1.2017.0.4.rationale: A picking game is governed by integer representability as a difference of squares.

uk1.2018.0.4.rationale: A real quadratic recurrence has alternative branches whose distinct attainable endpoint values are counted.

uk1.2018.0.6.rationale: A stopping arrangement must keep every partial mean integral.

uk1.2019.0.1.rationale: Count distinct digit assignments subject to divisibility by three.

uk1.2019.0.2.rationale: The circle supplies cyclic order. Consecutive integer triple products impose arithmetic constraints, without lengths or angles.

uk1.2019.0.3.rationale: Two factorizations with prescribed differences form a Diophantine problem.

uk1.2019.0.5.rationale: Similarity connects cylinder dimensions, surface areas and volumes to an algebraic system.

uk1.2019.0.6.rationale: Counting closed lattice walks is combined with the exact power of ten dividing their number.

uk1.2020.0.2.rationale: An integer quadratic recurrence reduces to arithmetic transitions; both recurrence algebra and integrality matter.

uk1.2020.0.4.rationale: A permutation is built by insertions determined by proper divisors.

uk1.2020.0.5.rationale: The circular layout defines a finite adjacency graph. Sweet-transfer reachability has integer-state constraints; no metric circle property is used.

uk1.2021.0.1.rationale: An affine integer iteration must return to the initial value.

uk1.2021.0.2.rationale: Triangle area and perimeter formulas are combined with integer b and perimeter conditions.

uk1.2021.0.3.rationale: Count sequences of geometric folds up to shape congruence. Congruent shapes do not imply modular arithmetic.

uk1.2021.0.7.rationale: A pebble game on integer positions has a terminal parity winning condition.

uk1.2022.0.1.rationale: Representations by consecutive odd integers depend on arithmetic sum and divisor conditions.

uk1.2022.0.2.rationale: An extremal win/loss history must realise exact rational percentages with integer denominators.

uk1.2022.0.3.rationale: Count bounded-multiplicity representations of an integer by binary powers.

uk1.2022.0.5.rationale: Minimise an algebraic mean over distinct positive integer sets, then test the minimum for integrality.

uk1.2022.0.6.rationale: Count integer recurrence choices producing a prescribed total sum.

uk1.2023.0.1.rationale: Leading-digit frequencies impose an integer quotient condition on the endpoint of an interval.

uk1.2023.0.2.rationale: An algebraic integer recurrence is optimised for the number of perfect-square terms.

uk1.2023.0.5.rationale: Divisibility chains are counted and their count must have arbitrarily specified divisors.

uk1.2024.0.1.rationale: Count permutations subject to one-sided displacement restrictions.

uk1.2024.0.2.rationale: Linear recurrence alternatives scale the adjacent integer difference, giving an arithmetic invariant.

uk1.2024.0.4.rationale: A positive-integer exponential expression is required to be a perfect square.

uk1.2024.0.5.rationale: Faults depend only on colours and cyclic index distances; no metric circle property is used.

uk1.2025.0.1.rationale: A cyclic arrangement must realise an induced cycle in the integer divisibility graph.

uk1.2025.0.2.rationale: Affine updates depend on the permutation through an alternating sum; the task combines algebraic cancellation and discrete arrangement.

uk1.2025.0.3.rationale: An impartial game replaces an integer factorisation by a difference, combining strategy and arithmetic structure.

uk1.2025.0.6.rationale: Colour selection is combined with equal Euclidean distances between cube centres.

uk1.2026.0.3.rationale: Count geometric tilings of a square using oriented L-shaped pieces.

uk1.2026.0.5.rationale: Reachability of all integers is governed by parity and rounded division in the integer iteration.

uk1.2026.0.6.rationale: Lily pads are cyclic positions for a peg-elimination game; arithmetic step invariants matter, but metric geometry does not.
